messages:
incident-bot: Pager: high-error-rate in routing layer (edge-us-east). Detected spike of 5xx responses and unexpected model fallbacks. Severity: P1. Paging on-call: @maria. Links: logs://logshare/edge-spillover/2334567890, runbook: /playbooks/routing-fallback

maria: acked. moving to incident channel. pinging @alex for routing rules, @ryan for infra, @kim for runtime.

alex: on it. currently seeing spillover from eu->us-east queues. initial telemetry shows region capacity oversubscription then fallback to lower-tier models.

ryan: I can try to rehydrate capacity but need policy decision on immediate manual routing cut. what's the customer impact?

maria: customer-impact: ~12% of requests to hosted API got >1s additional latency and ~4% got response mismatch (fallback model). A handful of premium customers reported errors. See summary in logs link above.

kim: quick note: runtime reports KV cache thrashing at 16:08:02 UTC, lots of cache invalidations across edge shards. Might trigger model variant selection mismatch.

alex: hypothesis H1: capacity spill -> automated spillover routed requests to edge-us-east fallback pool which has model-compat mismatches causing misroutes. H2: KV cache eviction caused prompt context loss -> downstream fallback to shorter context model.

janet: product: which customers impacted? any enterprise with dedicated capacity? we need to notify CSMs.

maria: three impacted tenants flagged: corp-alpha, beta-saas, gamma-analytics. corp-alpha saw partial failures for their longchat route.

ryan: I'm attaching a short log dump.

ryan: ```
# excerpt from edge shard 12
2026-03-15T16:07:58Z WARN route-alloc: spillover triggered to fallback-pool-us-east
2026-03-15T16:08:02Z ERROR kvcache: eviction-ratio=0.78 keys_evicted=4200
2026-03-15T16:08:03Z INFO model-switch: selected=fallback-quant-v1.3 compat_score=0.62
2026-03-15T16:08:07Z ERROR inference: misroute-detected input_hash=0x8f3a
```

alex: thanks. timeline so far (building):
- 16:07:58 UTC: upstream load spike detected on eu-region causing cross-region reroute policy to engage (spillover).
- 16:08:02 UTC: KV cache eviction spike on edge-us-east shard 12.
- 16:08:03 UTC: routing decision engine selects fallback-quant-v1.3 for a subset of sessions.
- 16:08:05 UTC: 4xx/5xx error rate increases to 6% for affected endpoints.
- 16:08:10 UTC: incident bot paged on-call.

maria: mitigation applied: temporary hard-route rule to prevent eu->us-east spillover at 16:09:30 UTC, and we disabled automatic fallback to quantized model for sensitive routes at 16:10:10 UTC. That reduced errors to baseline by 16:12:00 UTC.

kim: follow-up from runtime: the fallback-quant-v1.3 had a tokenizer model-id mismatch for some inputs which produced empty candidates in ~0.3% of cases. We should expand model-compat checks.

alex: we rolled out an emergency routing patch: set policy "prefer-local" for eu origin traffic and disabled tier-tiebreaker for 10m. ops-bot: deployed patch id = deploy-2334 at 16:09:28 UTC.

ops-bot: Deploy succeeded: deploy-2334 applied to routing-service (3/3 regions) in 42s.

janet: notify CSMs and affected customers. Draft message: "We've observed transient routing fallbacks leading to degraded responses. Mitigation applied; investigating root cause and we will follow up with RCA." Agree?

maria: yes. I'll coordinate with support. Also tagging for RCA: please add logs and eval prompts that showed misroutes.

alex: action items (triage thread):
- [A1] logs: collect full log window 16:05:00-16:15:00 across eu and us-east (assigned to ryan)
- [A2] evals: gather prompt samples that landed on fallback-quant-v1.3 (assigned to kim)
- [A3] policy: add stricter model-compat check to routing decision path (assigned to alex)
- [A4] customer comms: janet/maria

ryan: pulling logs now. linking artifact: logs://logshare/edge-spillover/2334567890/full-dump.tar.gz

kim: running evals on fallback-quant-v1.3 sample set. preliminary: mismatch rate higher for long-context prompts >1024 tokens.

maria: oncall handoff: my shift ends in 32 minutes. @alex please be ready to handoff if this resurfaces. I'll create a clean timeline and put notes into the incident doc.

alex: will take over. quick note for RCA thread: hypothesis priority H1>H2. We should also consider H3: autoscaler mis-estimated EU capacity due to short-lived burst pattern. Ryan can you check autoscaler logs?

ryan: checking. autoscaler shows several scale-up requests delayed by median 18s due to quota throttling for the pool at 16:07:50-16:08:20 UTC. attaching snippet.

ryan: ```
2026-03-15T16:07:49Z INFO autoscale: request=start pool=eu-primary
2026-03-15T16:07:51Z WARN quota: throttle=true reason=burst-protection
2026-03-15T16:08:01Z INFO autoscale: request=fulfilled
```

alex: that aligns. provisional root cause: short EU burst + quota throttling prevented timely scale-up -> spillover to us-east -> KV cache thrash + fallback to quantized model with partial compatibility -> client-visible misroutes.

maria: recording RCA notes in incident doc. tagging for followup: improve spillover policy (prefer local fallback pool with verified model compatibility), increase autoscaler headroom for eu-primary, and expand runtime model-compat checks before selecting quantized fallback.

janet: recommend post-incident customer follow-up for corp-alpha and beta-saas with timeline and mitigation steps.

alex: ok. I'll file a postmortem draft and include the action items and owners. ETA for draft: EOD.

maria: handing off on-call to @alex now. I will remain on standby for escalations. thanks all. :heart:

alex: taking over. closing live mitigation thread. will open RCA PR with timelines, logs, and eval artifacts.

ops-bot: Incident closed (soft) at 16:20:00 UTC. Please complete postmortem checklist: /playbooks/postmortem-checklist

maria: thanks team.
